scope: Manual comparison of the remaining twelve interfaces of aos-2024-v52-i01-p0285 against the pinned mathlib source, retaining the frozen census and its ambient-convention notes.

rows.query: Searched Probability, Analysis/Convex and LinearAlgebra for grouping, fusion and sparsity; inspected Function.support, Finset.filter and Finset.card bodies.
rows.result: Finite nonzero-coordinate support and its cardinality are available; the grouped parameter set can be assembled with a finite gamma witness and coordinate membership predicates.
rows.gap: Define the existential gamma constraint and concatenate unrestricted alpha, retaining upper bounds rather than exactly K occupied nonzero groups.

comparisons.D2: On Fin p, support beta is precisely the nonzero coordinate set and the cardinality of the corresponding filtered univ is the printed l0 count; alpha in R^q has no support bound. The ambient source review interprets the unquantified gamma in R^K as a feasibility witness. Its entries may repeat or vanish, so the construction gives at most K nonzero values and at most s nonzero coordinates, not K distinct occupied groups. Classical decidability handles exact real equality without a numerical tolerance. No sparsity penalty or design assumption belongs to this parameter set.

rows.query: Searched for grouped regression and L0-Fusion; inspected gaussianReal variance and zero-variance branch, iIndepFun, IdentDistrib and mulVec definitions.
rows.result: Scalar Gaussian errors, iid random observation triples and the finite linear predictor have separate library ingredients, but no verified declaration combines the latent coefficient grouping with this regression experiment.
rows.gap: Assemble the regression law and hidden distinct nonzero coefficient values without adding error-covariate independence absent from the source passage.

comparisons.D1: gaussianReal 0 with nonnegative variance sigma squared gives the stated marginal error law; iIndepFun and pairwise IdentDistrib of the full observation triples express iid sampling. Neither implies that the error within a triple is independent of X and Z, and no conditional Gaussian likelihood is inferred. Finite dot products give X beta plus Z alpha. The true gamma-star values are different and nonzero here, in contrast to the permissive gamma feasibility witness in D2; nuisance alpha is unrestricted. A high-dimensional sparsity motivation is not by itself an extra fixed-design or support-size hypothesis.

rows.query: Inspected Finset.filter, image including deduplication and membership, and card; searched grouping-specific interfaces in Probability and LinearAlgebra.
rows.result: Filtering coordinates by exact value and taking the deduplicated finite image of their nonzero fibers supplies the two grouping operators and their different cardinalities.
rows.gap: Assemble nonempty nonzero value fibers as a finite set of coordinate sets, keeping the zero fiber available only to the index operator.

comparisons.D3: The index set G(beta;r) is Finset.univ filtered by beta j = r and is valid also for r = 0 or an absent value. The grouping set consists of distinct nonempty fibers for realized r unequal to zero; Finset.image deduplicates the same fiber reached through several coordinates. Its cardinality counts coefficient classes, whereas the fiber cardinality counts coordinates. Equality is exact, the classes are unlabeled coordinate sets, and neither a tolerance nor zero-group inclusion is introduced.

rows.query: Searched Probability for grouping risk and inspected Measure.real with finite-measure convention plus finite fiber/filter/image operations.
rows.result: Real event probability under a probability measure can be applied to inequality of the two finite grouping sets; no specialized estimator is necessary.
rows.gap: Define the measurable grouping-error event for the supplied estimator and sampling law.

comparisons.D9: The event is inequality of unlabeled nonzero-coordinate partitions G(beta-hat) and G(beta-star); alpha does not affect it, and changing coefficient magnitudes without changing the groups incurs no grouping error. It ranges over any estimator, not just a minimizer of D6. Measure.real yields an ordinary number in [0,1] for a probability law; its infinite-mass-to-zero totalization is irrelevant only after that law is supplied. Event measurability should be justified from estimator measurability and finitely many equality tests, not obtained from the bare measure evaluation.

rows.query: Searched for group-matching distance and inspected the to_dual-generated Finset.min' signature, finite filters and cardinalities.
rows.result: A nonempty finite set of injection costs admits an attained minimum, but the injection family and the source's unmatched-coordinate objective need construction.
rows.gap: Construct injections from the smaller nonzero grouping to the larger and minimize the printed unmatched-coordinate count without symmetrizing it.

comparisons.D4: The domain condition card G(beta) <= card G(beta-prime) makes finite injections possible, including the unique empty-domain map. For each injection, the cost counts coordinates in the union of second-grouping classes outside the union of matched intersections G1 intersect f(G1). Filtering the finite coordinate universe encodes that set expression; Finset.min' applies after proving the finite cost set nonempty. No zero class is added. Swapping beta and beta-prime is neither always permitted nor certified to preserve the result, and generic metric axioms do not follow from the word distance.

rows.query: Searched for grouping sensitivity and least-squares separation; inspected mulVec, EuclideanSpace.norm_eq and IsMinOn with its separate membership condition.
rows.result: The finite prediction norm and a minimizer predicate are available; the parameter-indexed grouping sensitivity and attainment are not verified library constructions.
rows.gap: Build the mismatched-grouping feasible set and normalized prediction objective, resolving empty or unattained minima rather than totalizing them silently.

comparisons.D5: Use X times (beta-beta-star) plus Z times (alpha-alpha-star) in the n-dimensional Euclidean norm, squared, divided by n times max(d(beta,beta-star),1). The candidate class has group count at most the truth's count, so the directed injection distance is used in its valid orientation. X and Z are deterministic matrix arguments and no Gaussian law is needed. Positive sample size and the max with one address the displayed denominator but do not ensure the mismatch class is nonempty or its minimum attained. IsMinOn can certify a supplied feasible minimizer, not manufacture c_min from an arbitrary real infimum fallback.

rows.query: Inspected ConvexOn including convexity of its domain, the Riesz-map gradient definition and zero fallback, LipschitzOnWith and IsMinOn.
rows.result: Ambient objective convexity, a lower bound, and a Euclidean Lipschitz-gradient condition restricted to the feasible set can be stated separately; convexity of the sparse feasible set is not available.
rows.gap: Combine ambient convexity and a lower bound with a differentiable gradient Lipschitz only on Theta(K,s), without asserting that this generally nonconvex feasible set is convex.

comparisons.D12: ConvexOn R univ g is the natural ambient convex-objective ingredient; using ConvexOn R Theta g would additionally demand convexity of the grouped/sparse domain and would strengthen the source. Encode the universal lower bound C2 separately, and use LipschitzOnWith of the genuine gradient restricted to Theta with positive l and Euclidean geometry. gradient is totalized to zero where no Frechet derivative exists, so bare Lipschitzness of that total function cannot replace the source's differentiable-gradient meaning. D12 supplies no squared-loss or Gaussian specialization and no global minimizer existence. Its restricted bound also does not justify a first update from the arbitrary infeasible initialization recorded for the later algorithm.

rows.query: Searched Probability, Analysis and LinearAlgebra for L0-Fusion, lasso and least-squares; inspected finite prediction, support, Euclidean norm and IsMinOn definitions.
rows.result: The global constrained squared-error objective can be assembled, but no verified specialized fusion solver or selection theorem implements this optimization interface.
rows.gap: Define the joint alpha/beta/gamma feasible minimization with upper bounds on group count and beta support, and handle minimizer selection explicitly.

comparisons.D6: The objective is the unnormalized sum of n squared residuals, equivalent to the squared Euclidean residual norm. Gamma is optimized over R^K and supplies candidate coefficient levels including zero; repeated or unused levels remain allowed. The indicator sum counts nonzero beta coordinates only. IsMinOn plus membership expresses a global solution, without a unique minimizer, MIO implementation, preliminary screening, or penalty in place of the constraints. Gaussian model and independent observations describe the statistical context, but they do not certify optimization success.

rows.query: Searched grouping sensitivity subclasses and inspected the constituent prediction norm and minimizer predicate used in D5.
rows.result: The lower sensitivity threshold is a set predicate once the source-specific c_min is defined; no linear-subspace property or specialized sensitivity class was verified.
rows.gap: Form the subset of Theta(K0,s0) with c_min at least ell, retaining the unresolved minimum conventions inherited from c_min.

comparisons.D10: The parameter theta must satisfy the upper-bound group/support class and its own design-dependent c_min(theta,X,Z) >= ell with ell > 0. The author's word subspace does not assert closure under addition or scalar multiplication, so a Lean Submodule would be unjustified. X and Z remain fixed arguments, and no probabilistic assumption belongs to this subclass definition. The linked declarations support only c_min's underlying objective/minimizer relation; they neither define c_min nor resolve empty or unattained minima.

rows.query: Searched balanced grouping and coefficient separation; inspected finite exact-value filters and cardinalities.
rows.result: The absolute coordinate separation and multiplicative size comparisons are finite predicates, but the source's K0-indexed level labels require care within an at-most-K0 parameter class.
rows.gap: Assemble the separation and balance predicates while preserving the unresolved gamma-star labels and avoiding an unstated exact group-count assumption.

comparisons.D11: Every pair of unequal beta-star coordinates must differ by at least one, including a nonzero value versus an actually present zero coordinate; there is no condition against zero if no coordinate has that value. Size comparisons are card G(beta-star;gamma-k-star) <= 2 times card G(beta-star;gamma-k-prime-star) for all named levels. They exclude the zero class in their intended nonzero-group reading, but the source review flags that Theta is only an upper-bound class while labels run through K0. Keep that issue explicit rather than requiring exactly K0 occupied groups or dividing by a possibly empty group's size. The subclass is not asserted to be linear.

rows.query: Searched groupwise collapsed matrices; inspected matrix product entrywise summation and exact-value coordinate filters.
rows.result: Multiplying X by the coordinate-to-group incidence matrix produces one sum of original columns per nonzero group.
rows.gap: Choose the nonzero-group column enumeration and define its incidence matrix, with sums rather than averages.

comparisons.D7: Let the p-by-group incidence entry equal one when coordinate k is in the selected nonzero class and zero otherwise. Matrix.mul_apply identifies X times that matrix with the displayed column sum. The zero class supplies no output column, no group-size normalization is used, and an ordering of the otherwise unlabeled groups is needed to interpret gamma coordinates consistently. This deterministic design construction does not require full rank or Gaussian noise and says nothing about whether fitted coefficients remain distinct and nonzero.

rows.query: Searched least-squares and groupwise regression; inspected IsMinOn, finite matrix-vector prediction and squared Euclidean norm, and compared both archived oracle formulas.
rows.result: Each squared-loss minimizer relation can be stated, but generic least-squares primitives do not establish the asserted equivalence between exact grouping constraints and unrestricted collapsed regression.
rows.gap: Retain both oracle formulations and their possible discrepancy when fitted group coefficients merge or vanish, with existence and selection conditions explicit.

comparisons.D8: The first oracle minimizes over parameters with exactly the same nonzero coordinate groups as beta-star, which requires fitted group values to be distinct and nonzero and true-zero coordinates to stay zero. The second minimizes without these level constraints over R^(K0+q), then assigns fitted gamma values back to each true class. Such fitted values may coincide or equal zero, violating the first constraint; full column rank alone would not prevent that. IsMinOn with separate membership represents either formulation but does not identify them, choose a unique solution, or ensure attainment on the group-equality set. Preserve the source discrepancy rather than adding rank or nonzero-fit assumptions.
